To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the lymphocyte the synthesis of polypeptides is initiated in the small-sized particles, which have a sedimentation coefficient 80 S and less and buoyant density 134, 150 and 160 g/cm3 and is continued in the polysomes, which have sedimentation coefficient 130 S and more and buoyant density of 155 g/cm3.
the protein synthesis in mouse spleen lymphocytes proceeds in the course of the conversion of informosomes with monoribosomes to polysomes.
the synthesis of protein in lymphocytes occurs in a two-step manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the protein synthesizing structures in the lymphocytes and with the kinetics of protein synthesis in them.
the properties of the cytoplasmic mRNA particles from mouse spleen lymphocytes and the kinetics of their protein synthesis.
the study of the kinetics of the protein synthesis in mouse spleen lymphocytes and the properties of the cytoplasmic messenger ribonucleoprotein (mRNP) particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protein synthesizing structures of the lymphocytes are not only ribosomes but also mRNP particles, the complexes of ribosomes and mRNP particles with different sedimentation coefficients and buoyan density.
the protein synthesis in mouse splenic lymphocytes is a continuous process and occurs on polysomes, which have different buoyant density.
in lymphocytes the protein biosynthesis proceeds in the following sequence of stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the protein synthesis in the mouse lymphocytes proceeds in the course of the formation of the complexes between the small-sized informosomes and the single ribosomes and then in the course of polysome formation.

the lymphocytes contain two types of protein synthesizing complexes with different properties: (a) complexes with single ribosomes (informosomes), which are able to synthesize polypeptides, and (b) polysomes, which are able to continue the polypeptide synthesis and to synthesize proteins.

the protein synthesis in lymphocytes proceeds in the following manner: the informosomes with single free ribosomes are involved into the protein synthesis first, and then the informosomes are transformed into polysomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the time of the translation of the polypep-tide chains in the polysomes is 30 sec and that of the polypeptidic chain translation in the small-sized particles, in the medium-sized ones and in the informosome complexes with single ribosomes is 5-15 sec.
the protein synthesis in lymphocytes is carried out on ribosomes of two kinds, the large-sized and the small-sized ones, the latter having a low buoyant density.

the protein synthesizing structures of lymphocytes are heterogeneous and the protein synthesis in these cells proceeds in two phases: the first one in the complexes of the informosomes with single or few ribosomes, and the second in the polysomes.
